title: The Catechism, again
tomorrow: can someone this competitive actually be holy?

lines: A LOGO TELLS YOU WHAT'S INSIDE.
MUSIC ON A BOOK OF DOCTRINE?
cards: Band merch, team crests, the little icon on every app: a logo is supposed to tell you what's inside. So look at the logo on the Catechism of the Catholic Church, a thick book of what the Church teaches.
It isn't a key, a seal or a gavel. It's a shepherd sitting under a tree, playing a set of pipes, with a sheep resting at his feet. Why put music on the cover of a book of doctrine?

teach.b: The Catechism explains its own logo. The picture comes from an old Christian tombstone in the catacombs of Domitilla, in Rome. Christians used it for the rest and happiness of a soul with God.

The book reads it like this: Christ the Good Shepherd leads his flock with his staff, draws them with the music of truth, the pipes, and lets them rest in the shade of the tree of life, which is his cross.
So before you read a single line, the cover makes a claim: this book wants to be heard, like a voice you trust, not just looked up like a dictionary.
Jesus says in John, in the Douay-Rheims Bible, "My sheep hear my voice." Inside, the music has four movements, the four pillars. The first is what Catholics believe, walked through the Creed.
The second is how they celebrate, in the sacraments. The third is how they live, with the commandments. The fourth is how they pray, built around the Our Father.
Here's the one to tell a friend: a book that big, full of doctrine and law, doesn't end on a rule. Its last part is about prayer, and its very last paragraph is about one word: Amen.
The four hold each other up. Take one away and the others lean. Belief with no prayer goes dry; prayer with no life goes soft.
That's why the shepherd plays one song, not four.

how: The Catechism of the Catholic Church is organized in four parts: the profession of faith, the celebration of the Christian mystery, life in Christ, and Christian prayer. Catholics use it for study, teaching and preparing for the sacraments.

games.q: a friend wants to understand Catholics and asks where the Catechism starts. which part would you open first for her?
o: what Catholics believe, walked through the Creed.
a list of sins, arranged from worst to least.
the history of every pope, in order.
games.why: the first pillar is the profession of faith, built on the Creed. then celebrate, live and pray follow.

practice: Move slowly through the four with your body: a hand on your heart for believe, both hands open for celebrate, your feet pressed into the floor for live, palms together for pray.
Then choose one pillar for this month, and keep that posture while the sit runs.
